summary.text: A male Boxer aged 8 years presented with progressive paraparesis. Blood tests were unremarkable. MRI with gadolinium contrast showed a T9-T10 intramedullary spinal cord mass, described for dogs 1 to 5 as well circumscribed and iso- to mildly hyperintense on T2WI with marked edema, marked homogeneous and strong ring contrast enhancement.

The dog was euthanized due to a poor prognosis and the tumor was sampled post-mortem. Histology showed a biphasic tumor with Table 3 grades (moderate cellularity, marked capillary component, mild inflammatory component, mild vacuolization, moderate desmoplasia) and extensive inflammatory aggregates surrounding the tumor on the subgross section. The tumor was INHα negative, CAIX positive and had scattered GFAP positive cells.

Dog 6: Residual nerve fibers show different degrees of axonal and myelin degeneration (LFB). Bar = 100 µm.

article_limitations: Veterinary case series of six dogs (five spinal cord hemangioblastomas and one sciatic nerve case); each dog is a roster patient numbered by the dog label order in the neurological signs sentence. Breed is kept only in case context because the demographics schema has no breed attribute.

Cohort, literature and discussion statements were not copied to individuals: the abstract, mean age, breed counts, the 1 to 3 year follow-up range, the 4 no-recurrence count, the 5 to 11 mm tumor size range, the unlabelled subgroup counts of 2 and 3 dogs by tumor compartment, the unlabelled histology and immunohistochemistry sentences, the Ki-67 range, Tables 4 and 5 and the two Cornell cases.

Sentences that explicitly cover all dogs or all tumors (blood tests, MRI protocol, biphasic histology, INHα negativity, CAIX positivity) were copied to each dog with the covering wording in the evidence.

Source conflicts recorded as review-only pairs: dog 2 cellularity (Table 3 moderate versus Figure 3b highly cellular) and dog 2 post-contrast T1WI enhancement pattern (dogs 1-5 text homogeneous versus Figure 1b heterogeneous). Dog 1 inflammation (Table 3 mild intratumoral grade versus Figure 3a extensive peritumoral aggregates) describes different attributes and is kept as supported items with an ambiguity note (parent review).
Table 2 Outcome cell for dog 1 is a dash; the text states euthanasia. Dog 4 owners elected euthanasia but death is not stated literally.
The Figure 4 caption lists panels e and h under spinal cord while labeling them dog 6 (sciatic nerve case); no tissue site is recorded for those observations.
Supplement ZIP contains an image of control ovary tissue (Figure S1) and a video of the dog 2 resection (Video S1); neither adds transcribed clinical facts.
Dog 6 presenting signs are stated for the left pelvic limb while the tumor is in the right sciatic nerve; recorded as an ambiguity, both kept as written.

Video S1 (inside the ZIP) opens with C5 and C6 vertebral labels and a segment showing an anatomical spine model with a pointer before the intraoperative footage, and ends with an organization end card; its audio track is digitally silent (ffmpeg volume detection: mean -91 dB, maximum -90.3 dB). No clinical facts are transcribed from it.
